body_content:
Hi Steven

 

The cost of the goods should be invoiced separately to any planning,design,R&D etc install this should all be invoiced separately it is not relevant to the import of the lift.

If you were to just supply the lift and they install themselves the price of the item is the price of the item..

 

CTH :84281020

DESCRIPTION FOR CTH:      OTHER LIFTING, HANDLING, LOADING OR UNLOADING MACHINERY (FOR EXAMPLE, LIFTS, ESCALATORS, CONVEYORS, TELEFERICS);  Lifts and skip hoists;  Skip hoists;  

 

Custom Duty: BCD 7.5% SWC 10% IGST 18% (app 28.465%)

 

This would be calculated on CIF so important to include the cost of freight and insurance to the value before doing nay calcs.. this would all be paid by the importer not you on DAP basis.

 

 

Colin Redman

Subject: KNMA Delhi customs valuation and import duty confirmation

Hi Jordan and Charlie,

We are working on an export to the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art in New Delhi and I would like to get the Indian import duty position properly confirmed before we give the client a figure.

Giles has already been looking at the shipping with you and we have been working on the basis of the previous Transport House shipment.

The shipment is a bespoke Sesame platform lift, being shipped by sea to New Delhi on a DAP basis.

The proposed commodity code is 8428 10 20 00.

The question I need professional confirmation on is what value Indian Customs will actually use for calculating the import duties and taxes.

Our overall contract includes a significant amount of UK engineering, design, manufacturing labour and installation work. It is not simply £180,000 worth of materials arriving in India.

Our current breakdown gives us approximately:

Full project value used in the initial calculation: approximately £180,679.75. I have attached the current quote being used at tender stage, the final order quote will need to be created and that can be clearer to reduce the import duties with your advice.

Value after removing our UK labour hours but including install costs which includes shipping and install labour: £99,019.75

Equipment and materials only: £63,708.75

Could you please check this with whoever handles your Indian customs clearance, ideally your Indian customs broker or destination agent, and confirm the following for us:

  1. Can the assessable customs value be based on the £63,708.75 value of the physical equipment being imported, provided our commercial documentation clearly separates the equipment from engineering, design, installation and commissioning services?
  1. Does any of our UK engineering or manufacturing labour have to be included in the customs value because it contributes to the manufacture of the equipment, even where it is shown separately on the contract or invoice?
  1. Can installation and commissioning services carried out in India by our engineers be excluded from the import customs value?
  1. Does the freight cost need to be added to the assessable value for Indian Customs even though the shipment is being supplied DAP?
  1. Is 8428 10 20 00 the correct classification for this type of platform lift equipment going into India?
  1. What Basic Customs Duty, Social Welfare Surcharge, IGST and any other statutory charges would actually apply once the correct assessable value has been established?
  1. Is the IGST paid at import normally recoverable by a GST registered Indian importer as input tax credit? We want to distinguish between an import cash payment and a genuine non recoverable project cost.
  1. How would you recommend we structure the commercial invoice, contract and service elements so that Indian Customs can clearly see the value of the physical equipment separately from the services?

We have seen indicative calculations online, but I do not want to rely on those for something of this value. I would much rather have the position confirmed by the people who would actually clear the goods into India.

If possible, could you get your Indian customs agent or broker to look at this specific example and give us the basis they would use?

Once we have that answer, we can give the client a sensible, landed cost rather than assuming duties and taxes apply to the complete Sesame contract value.

Regards,

 

Steven Lyons

 

Sesame Access Systems Ltd

Unit 1

Cumberland Works

Wintersells Business Park

West Byfleet

KT147LF

 

Tel: 01784 904490

Web:www.sesameaccess.com
